paper_type_evidence.quote: We attempt to observe CO(2–1), $^{13}$CO(2–1), and C$^{18}$O(2–1) line polarization toward HD 142527 and IM Lup, which are large, bright protoplanetary disks.

claims.result: Q signal in CO(2-1) in both disks (SNR_Q 8.7 and 9.6), with comparable off-disk SNR in Monte Carlo; no U or V signal and no signal in 13CO or C18O
claims.finding: The CO(2-1) Stokes Q signals are marginal detections, insufficient to infer a polarization or field pattern

evidence.quote: Our Monte Carlo simulations indicate that these signals are marginal.
The polarization signal for both disks is found for Stokes $Q$ only

claims.hypothesis: Keplerian-rotation stacking of Stokes parameters reveals line polarization
claims.experiment: GoFish stacking over whole disks and 90 deg quadrants with a range of radii and wedges
claims.result: No significant signal in Stokes Q, U, V
claims.finding: No polarization found by stacking; it yields 3 sigma Pfrac upper limits ~0.2-3.3% depending on line and region

evidence.quote: We also stack Stokes parameters based on the Keplerian rotation, but no signal was found.
we could not find a significant signal in Stokes $Q$, $U$, and $V$ via stacking.

claims.hypothesis: Line polarization fraction can be constrained across the disks at the observing resolution
claims.experiment: Per-pixel 3 sigma upper limits over velocity intervals of 0.5-1.5 km/s and stacked upper limits
claims.result: Pixel-wise limits typically <3-4% for CO and 13CO and up to 12% for C18O in IM Lup; stacking gives limits up to a factor ~10 lower
claims.finding: Line polarization in these disks is low; stacking limits may hide small-scale structure

evidence.quote: Upper limits based on our stacking technique are up to a factor of $\sim$10 lower, though stacking areas can potentially average out small-scale polarization structure.

claims.hypothesis: 1.3 mm continuum polarization differs from 870 um polarization in HD 142527 and IM Lup
claims.experiment: Compared 1.3 mm polarization with re-imaged archival (HD 142527) and published (IM Lup) 870 um data at common resolution
claims.result: HD 142527 north shows a changed morphology and Pfrac ratio up to ~5 with angle differences up to 90 deg; IM Lup 1.3 mm is more azimuthal with Pfrac ratio mostly >1
claims.finding: Significant wavelength dependence; consistency with scattering needs detailed modeling

evidence.quote: The polarization in the northern dust trap of HD 142527 shows a significant change in morphology and an increase in $P_{\text{frac}}$ as compared to 870 $\mu$m.

claims.hypothesis: The optical depths of the CO isotopologues favour 13CO and C18O for detecting GK polarization
claims.experiment: Line-ratio optical depth maps with fixed isotopic ratios
claims.result: CO(2-1) tau typically >30 (HD 142527) or ~40 (IM Lup); 13CO ~1-7; C18O 0.1-1
claims.finding: Optical depth alone favours 13CO and C18O but polarization was found only in CO(2-1)

evidence.quote: Based on optical depth alone, we expect $^{13}$CO(2–1) and C$^{18}$O(2–1) to be optimal for probing the GK effect in these disks, while CO(2–1) is expected to be suboptimal.

why_this_data.value: Band 6 is the only band where CO, 13CO and C18O can be observed simultaneously; large bright disks with simple CO morphologies chosen

evidence.quote: We chose Band 6 because this is the only ALMA band where the spectral lines CO, $^{13}$CO, and C$^{18}$O can be observed simultaneously.
These two targets are among the largest and brightest known disks with simple CO morphologies.

why_this_method.value: Polarization is not obvious in the Stokes images, so stacking and spatial averaging over an integrated velocity range were used for a deeper search

evidence.loc: Searching for a Polarized Signal in Spectral Lines
evidence.quote: We decided to do a deeper search for a polarized signal via spectral stacking and via spatial averaging over an integrated velocity range.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: A vast mixture of wedges and radii was tried for stacking on all three lines; none gave a significant signal

evidence.quote: We tried a vast mixture of wedges and radii for all 3 spectral lines.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Velocity intervals above 1.5 km/s (2, 2.5, 3 km/s) give worse upper limits and were not reported

evidence.loc: Constraining the Polarization Percentage of the Observations
evidence.quote: Any higher velocity intervals (e.g., 2, 2.5, and 3 km s$^{-1}$) largely result in much worse upper limit sensitivities across the map.

limitations_admitted.value: Marginal Q detection only; inferring the magnetic field morphology is too difficult due to GK ambiguity and possible resonant scattering

evidence.loc: Searching for Signal within an Aperture
evidence.quote: Moreover, trying to infer the magnetic field morphology from these observations is too difficult, given the ambiguity of the GK effect

limitations_admitted.value: Stacking can average out small-scale polarization structure

evidence.quote: but we note that the stacking method can potentially average out small-scale polarization structure.

limitations_admitted.value: IM Lup phase center was offset 0.8'' west from the disk centre

evidence.quote: For IM Lup, the phase center of the observations was errantly located 0.8$''$ west from the disk center.

limitations_admitted.value: Only CO(2-1) Stokes Q marginal signals in each disk is peculiar and may indicate more complex noise behaviour than tested

evidence.loc: Searching for Signal within an Aperture
evidence.quote: finding a marginal signal for each disk only for CO(2–1) Stokes $Q$ is peculiar and may indicate a more complex noise behavior that could not be found with our tests.

referee_caveats_inferred: The aperture-search signal is selected by maximising SNR over position, size and channels; the Monte Carlo shows off-disk pixels reach similar SNR, so significance is not established
Abstract (1.57%) and text (1.56%) disagree on the HD 142527 CO polarization fraction
Stokes Q-only signal with no matching U or V could arise from instrumental leakage; leakage (D-term) calibration residuals are only bounded at <5% for polarization
Upper limits from stacking use the Stokes V stacked noise as the polarized-intensity noise, assuming V is noise-only
Disk geometry and stellar masses come from literature models without uncertainty propagation beyond a 1000-run perturbation

code_released.value: Custom aperture-search script described, no release or repository stated; GoFish is a cited public package

evidence.loc: Searching for Signal within an Aperture
evidence.quote: We then developed a script that alters the size and position of the circular aperture to find the location with the highest signal to noise.

missing_for_reproduction: The custom aperture-search script and its exact search grid
Full tclean parameters (niter, threshold, masks, image size, spectral grid) and line-free channel definitions
Calibration scripts and CASA version for the ARC manual calibration
Velocity ranges for the moment 0 maps and the pink integrated channels
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: About 10-50 GB for the single Band 6 execution of 2018.1.01172.S (1 hour per target, 46 antennas, a 2 GHz continuum plus three high-resolution line basebands); the 870 um comparison adds another dataset
reproducibility.score_reason: ALMA data (project 2018.1.01172.S) are archival and results are numeric, but imaging details, channel selections and the custom aperture-search script are not given, and the detection significance depends on those choices.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Data come from a single archived ALMA project, the main results are numeric (Pfrac, SNR_Q, upper limits) and the analysis algorithm (aperture SNR maximisation, GoFish stacking, upper-limit equation) is described in enough detail to redo approximately.

methods_papers.why: Channel covariance from Hanning smoothing and spectral averaging
Optical depth from brightness temperature ratio
